blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and September 2026, detached houses: listings rose from 86 in June to 98 in September (+14.0%), and it took 10.7% of the city’s 298 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings was 0 in June and 2 in September, too few (under 3) to call a rise or fall, and it took 0.0% of the city’s 558 sales over the period.

items.t: Brookswood is a sub-area of the Township of Langley, BC, inside the Brookswood-Fernridge community area; the Township plan name is the Brookswood-Fernridge Community Plan, covering the Booth, Fernridge and Rinn neighbourhoods.

Plan-area study boundaries (Township commercial market demand study for Booth, Fernridge and Rinn): bounded to the west by 196 Street, to the north by 33A Avenue, 200 Street, 36 Avenue, 208 Street and 43 Avenue, to the east by Murray Creek, 40 Avenue, 210 Street and 208 Street, and to the south by 20 Avenue, 198 Street and 16 Avenue. A street-level boundary for the board's Brookswood sub-area itself: UNVERIFIED — the board sub-area code is UNVERIFIED.

Brookswood's detached ratio of 7% is the lowest published detached ratio in the Langley set that month, and its detached inventory of 98 is the second-largest in the set, behind Willoughby Heights at 100. SnapStats publishes medians at community level only (Langley = City + Township combined), so no Brookswood-only median is published: per-sub-area medians are UNVERIFIED. Combined-Langley context only (NOT Brookswood figures): Detached median $1,345,000; Condos & Townhomes median $611,000.

Catchments: UNVERIFIED — SD35 catchments are address-based, and the sample address 20902 37A Avenue was run in the SD35 School Locator and returned NO RESULT, so no catchment is confirmed for any Brookswood address.

Transit: TransLink route 531 (Willowbrook / White Rock Centre) runs via 200 Street, 56 Avenue and Langley Centre; route 561 (Brookswood) runs Langley Centre to Brookswood; route 563 (Fernridge) runs Langley Centre to Fernridge; all three serve the stop at southbound 200 Street at 37A Avenue, and Langley Centre is the exchange. No SkyTrain or West Coast Express station is in Brookswood.

Parks and services: the Township lists Brookswood Park, Brookswood Skateboard Park, Noel Booth Community Park, Bell Park, Dale Ball Passive Park, East Brookswood Park, Highpoint Park, Rees-Callard Natural Park and Wiser Natural Area among Brookswood/Fernridge parks; George Preston Recreation Centre is at 20699 42 Avenue; Brookswood Library (Fraser Valley Regional Library) is at 20045 40 Avenue. Health care: Langley Memorial Hospital, 22051 Fraser Highway, is the nearest hospital confirmed on a health authority source; the nearest Urgent and Primary Care Centre is the Langley UPCC, 202 - 20434 64th Avenue.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Brookswood Guide

items.t: Township plans and zoning: the Brookswood-Fernridge Community Plan covers the area, with Booth, Fernridge and Rinn Neighbourhood Plans under it; the Township states the plan allows previously undeveloped areas to grow while protecting trees and watercourses. Zoning is Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw 1987 No. 2500: Section 110.1 as read in Township council reports sets SR-1 minimum lot area 3,716 m² (40 m frontage), SR-2 minimum 8,094 m² (45 m) and SR-3 minimum 1,765 m² (27.45 m); RU-2 minimums are UNVERIFIED from a readable bylaw section.

SSMUH — Township Bylaw 6020, stated correctly: Zoning Amendment Bylaw 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024) allows 3 units on eligible lots of 280 m² or smaller, 4 units on larger eligible lots up to 4,050 m²; lots over 4,050 m² are ineligible. There is NO 6-plex / 6-unit tier in the Township of Langley.

Secondary suites and coach houses (Township): the Township caps a secondary suite at 120 m² maximum gross floor area (Zoning Bylaw No. 2500, s. 102). A coach house in the Township is a fee-simple second unit under Zoning Bylaw 2500 s. 102 — it is NEVER strata and never a condo.

Pad rent (parks): where a Brookswood purchase is a park home, pad rent is governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act, not the Strata Property Act: the rent increase limit for manufactured home site tenancies is 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026 and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027, with 3 full months' notice and one increase per 12 months.

blocks.text: Good to know about Brookswood Guide

items.t: The "condo" shelf here is two listings deep.

(1) An open-house time conflict on the 20061 27 Avenue card — the card's time block reads "Nov 01, 2026, 02:00 PM – 04:00 PM PST" while the same card's listing text reads "Open House on Sunday, November 1, 2026 1:00PM - 3:00PM." (2) The guide's main FAQ block leaves "Are there golf courses near Brookswood?" unanswered in that block (an answer appears in a second FAQ block lower on the page).

Three of the area's best-known "communities" are pad-rental parks, not strata. Cedar Creek Estates (3031 200 St), Fernridge Park (20071 24 Ave) and Pineridge (2270 196 St) all record leasehold non-strata tenure in listings and publish 55+ rules — park rules under a tenancy act, with pad rent under the MHPTA increase formula (2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026; 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027), not strata fees under a Form B.
Cedar Lane is not Cedar Creek, and neither status should be borrowed. Deer Creek Estates is likewise held UNCONFIRMED. None is counted anywhere.

The school locator cannot place the secondary school's own address. The SD35 School Locator returned NO RESULT for 20902 37A Avenue — Brookswood Secondary's own address — because the address falls in a gap between the locator's listed ranges for 37A Avenue. A Brookswood school claim made without a locator run for the exact address is a guess.
The guide feed and the board count different Brookswoods. The two sources measure different sets at different moments, and neither should be quoted as the other.

Zoning minimums, not averages, frame Brookswood lots. Section 110.1 of Bylaw 2500 as read in Township council reports runs SR-3 at a 1,765 m² minimum up to SR-2 at 8,094 m² — a sub-area average lot size on an official source is UNVERIFIED, and a lot's subdivision story starts from its zone minimum, not from a neighbourhood average.

items.t: Strata block (bare-land strata parcels): Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions). blocks.text: Good to know about Brookswood

items.t: SSMUH eligibility in Brookswood is a servicing map, not a slogan (Township council report, June 10, 2024). The Township's own estimate puts Brookswood at ~15% of single-family/duplex lots eligible for 3–4 units, against ~99% in Walnut Grove — because eligibility follows existing municipal water and sewer.

A strata plan is a subdivision in the ALR — even with no building (ALC Information Bulletin 09). Filing a bare-land strata plan on reserve land triggers the same ALC permission requirement as a conventional subdivision.
The R-CL maximum is a LOT-area cap, not a floor-area cap (Bylaw 2500 s.403). R-CL runs 220 m² minimum lot area to 464.5 m² maximum lot area; a "355 m²" figure appears nowhere in the bylaw.
The feed and the board count different sets (Sep 2026).
Approved claims, as page statements only: REALTOR since 2015; 10 straight years FVREB Medallion Club; Top 1%; #1 in South Surrey/White Rock by MLS points 2025 + 2026 YTD; $500M+ sales.

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in Brookswood?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.

faq.q: Cedar Creek Estates shows up in condo searches — is it a condo?
faq.a: No. It is Cedar Creek Manufactured Home Park, 3031 200 Street, designated Manufactured Home Park in the Brookswood-Fernridge Community Plan; listings record the tenure as leasehold not prepaid-non-strata. You buy the home and rent the pad — no strata, no Form B.

faq.q: The parks say 55+ and no rentals. Are those rules void like strata rules?
faq.a: No — the November 24, 2022 voiding applies to strata rental-restriction bylaws. Park rules sit under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act and the park's own rules and tenancy agreement; a park's 55+ and no-rentals lines in listings are listing-stated park rules to confirm with the park, not void strata bylaws.

faq.q: How did Brookswood sell in September 2026?
faq.a: No Brookswood-only median is published; the combined Langley medians (detached $1,345,000; attached $611,000) blend in the City of Langley and the other Township sub-areas and are not Brookswood figures.

faq.q: Can I put six units on a Brookswood house lot?
faq.a: No. Township SSMUH under Bylaw 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024) allows 3 units on eligible lots of 280 m² or smaller and 4 units on larger eligible lots up to 4,050 m², and there is no 6-plex tier in the Township.

faq.q: Is Bromley a condo building, and is Brookswood Mills one?
faq.a: Bromley is not — it is a collection of 26 townhomes by Leone Homes at 4558 208 Street, selling as a presale with Phase 1 completion estimated Summer 2027.

faq.q: Cedar Creek Estates shows up in condo searches — is it a condo?
faq.a: No. It is Cedar Creek Manufactured Home Park, 3031 200 Street, designated Manufactured Home Park in the Brookswood-Fernridge Community Plan; listings record the tenure as leasehold not prepaid-non-strata. You buy the home and rent the pad — no strata, no Form B.

faq.q: The parks say 55+ and no rentals. Are those rules void like strata rules?
faq.a: No — the November 24, 2022 voiding applies to strata rental-restriction bylaws. Park rules sit under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act and the park's own rules and tenancy agreement; a park's 55+ and no-rentals lines in listings (Fernridge Park's listing states pets and rentals are not permitted, with park manager approval required) are listing-stated park rules to confirm with the park, not void strata bylaws.

faq.q: Can I put six units on a Brookswood house lot?
faq.a: No. Township SSMUH under Bylaw 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024) allows 3 units on lots up to 280 m² and 4 units on lots under 4,050 m², and there is no 6-plex tier in the Township — a claim of six as-of-right units on a Brookswood lot is wrong, and lots over 4,050 m² are ineligible for the SSMUH tiers at all.
